claims.text: In Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles, premelting extent and onset temperature are controlled primarily by particle-size-dependent surface-energy effects.
Particle-size-dependent surface-energy effects enhance atomic mobility at nanoparticle surfaces.
Particle-size-dependent surface-energy effects induce local compositional segregation at nanoparticle surfaces.
The initial Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles have homogeneous elemental distributions.
The initial Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles possess crystalline order.
Smaller nanoparticles have a substantially higher surface-to-volume ratio than larger nanoparticles.
Elevated surface energy in smaller nanoparticles lowers the premelting temperature through enhanced atomic mobility.
Local elemental redistribution contributes to lower-temperature premelting in smaller nanoparticles.
Surface effects are less dominant in larger Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles.
Larger nanoparticles exhibit a more abrupt, bulk-like melting transition.
Surface disorder and local atomic rearrangements act as precursors to complete melting.
Smaller nanoparticles will show a gradual onset of disorder during heating.
Premelting in smaller nanoparticles will begin approximately 10–20% lower in temperature than the sharp melting transition in larger nanoparticles.
Approximately 15 nm Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles are expected to exhibit minimal premelting and a well-defined melting point.

The proposed size-dependent mechanism is expected to hold for Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles approximately 2–20 nm in diameter under comparable heating rates and without extraneous environmental interactions.
Molecular-dynamics time-scale limitations may affect the inferred premelting onset.
A particle-size-independent premelting onset would falsify the proposed particle-size-dependent governing mechanism.
Nearly identical melting behavior in small and large nanoparticles, together with no significant surface segregation, would falsify the proposed mechanism.
